cli.governance.provider_observations.opt: Perform the planned operation and write its result. Without this flag the command only plans and prints; nothing durable changes.
Identifier of the approval that authorizes the write. Required when --apply needs an approval that is not already held.
Path to the observation database to operate on instead of the project default.
Digest of the plan this run must match. The operation is refused when the store has changed since that plan was produced.
Path to the observation preimage file to adopt. Read as evidence; the file itself is never modified.
Restrict reconciliation to this run identifier. Repeat the flag to reconcile several runs in one pass.
cli.governance.provider_observations.rec: Compare recorded observations against the runs they claim and report every mismatch. Plans by default; --apply writes the reconciliation.

cli.help:
Usage: {name} [--version|-v] [--help|-h]
  config get [key] [--json] [--global]
  policy vocabulary [--json]
  doctor [--json]
  paths [--global] [--json]
  run create --scope <id> --id <run> --command-id <id> --graph <file|-> [--json]
    [--lang en|tr] [--no-color]
  run reserve --scope <id> --id <run> --command-id <id> --expected-revision <n>
    [--json] [--lang en|tr] [--no-color]
  task execute --scope <id> --run <id> --task <id> --attempt <id>
    --generation <n> --layout-revision <id> [--json] [--lang en|tr] [--no-color]
  task evaluate --scope <id> --run <id> --task <id> --attempt <id>
    --generation <n> --layout-revision <id> --command-id <id>
    --expected-revision <n> [--json] [--lang en|tr] [--no-color]
  run inspect --scope <id> --id <run> [--json] [--lang en|tr] [--no-color]
  run cancel --scope <id> --id <run> --command-id <id> --expected-revision <n>
    [--json] [--lang en|tr] [--no-color]
  inventory --scope <id> [--after <id>] [--limit <n>] [--json] [--lang en|tr]
    [--no-color]
  --graph - reads graph JSON from piped stdin. --json writes one result to
    stdout; errors use stderr.
  Exit codes: 0 success, 1 operation error, 2 usage, 78 configuration.
  runtime serve [--json] [--lang en|tr] [--no-color]
Run/task and models invoke/invocation commands require this explicitly started local service.
  init preview --profile <file> [--allow-shutdown] [--json]
  models [--json]
  models binding|activation|activate|deactivate|invoke|invocation --help
cli.help.run:
Usage: deckent run <action>
  create --scope <id> --id <run> --command-id <id> --graph <file|-> [--json]
    [--lang en|tr] [--no-color]
  reserve --scope <id> --id <run> --command-id <id> --expected-revision <n>
    [--json] [--lang en|tr] [--no-color]
  inspect --scope <id> --id <run> [--json] [--lang en|tr] [--no-color]
  cancel --scope <id> --id <run> --command-id <id> --expected-revision <n>
    [--json] [--lang en|tr] [--no-color]
Run creation admits a graph; reservation selects Tasks and generates Attempt
    identities. Neither command executes Tasks or accepts a caller verdict.
cli.help.task:
Usage: deckent task <action>
  execute --scope <id> --run <id> --task <id> --attempt <id> --generation <n>
    --layout-revision <id> [--json] [--lang en|tr] [--no-color]
  evaluate --scope <id> --run <id> --task <id> --attempt <id> --generation <n>
    --layout-revision <id> --command-id <id> --expected-revision <n> [--json]
    [--lang en|tr] [--no-color]
Execution records terminal process evidence; evaluation decides Task acceptance
    from recorded evidence. A terminal result alone is not acceptance.

Read paths: `archive inspect`, `archive verify`, `archive terminal-inspect`, `archive terminal-verify`
  — they build projections over archived evidence and change no archive state.

Read paths: `audit <run-id>`, `audit query`, `audit compliance` — they only project stored audit events.
Mutation paths: `audit forward` writes an export target, `audit retention --apply` prunes or archives stored events.
Without --apply the retention path is a dry-run projection.

cli.memcat.usage.help.authority:
Authority: the token/limit table is parsed from Claude Code JSONL transcripts on this machine.
That is the only source it reads — no other provider transcript format is aggregated, so a
session run through another provider does not appear in this table.
`--lineage` switches to a different authority: archived task and result evidence, not transcripts.

cli.help.models:
Usage: deckent models [--json] [--lang en|tr] [--no-color]
Lists configured model declarations. Availability is not observed.
  models binding|activation|activate|deactivate --help
  models invoke|invocation|purge-content --input <file|-> [--json]
Invoke, invocation, and purge-content require an explicitly started local `deckent runtime serve`. A runtime-owned invocation continues if the client disconnects; retrying the same command identity returns its receipt and does not resend the native request.
models.notConfigured: Model catalog is not configured; availability was not observed.
models.availabilityNotObserved: Declarations only; availability was not observed.
mcp.tool.listDeclaredModels: List configured model declarations. This does not observe provider availability, credentials, activation, or execution readiness.
config.field.provider_catalog: Versioned native provider and model declarations; not activation or availability.
cli.help.modelsBinding:
Usage: deckent models binding --provider ID --provider-version VERSION --model ID --model-version VERSION [--json] [--lang LOCALE] [--no-color]
Inspect the exact declared native model definition and its SHA-256 content binding. This does not activate a model or authorize execution.
models.bindingNotDeclared: {reference}: exact model version is not declared in catalog {revision}.
models.bindingDeclared:
{reference} | catalog {revision} | native ID {nativeId} | SHA-256 {digest}
Declaration content binding only; no activation or execution authority.
mcp.tool.inspectModelBinding: Inspect one exact configured model declaration and its semantic binding digest. This does not observe availability, credentials, activation, or execution readiness.
mcp.tool.inspectModelActivation: Inspect scoped recorded model activation. This does not establish provider availability or invocation permission.
mcp.tool.admitModelActivation: Explicitly activate or deactivate an exact model under current policy. An idempotent replay returns historical evidence, not current state; no provider is invoked.
cli.help.modelsActivation:
Usage: deckent models activation|activate|deactivate --scope ID --provider ID --provider-version VERSION --model ID --model-version VERSION [--json] [--lang LOCALE] [--no-color]
activate/deactivate also require --command-id ID --expected-revision N --binding-digest SHA256. activate additionally requires --catalog-revision REV.
Inspect recorded state or submit an explicit activation command. This does not establish provider availability or invocation permission.
models.activation.absent: {reference} in scope {scope}: no persisted activation record; not activated.
models.activation.persisted: {reference} in scope {scope}: persisted {state} activation at revision {revision}.
models.activation.receipt: {replay}: command {command} recorded {state} activation for {reference} in scope {scope} at revision {revision}.
models.activation.notice: Recorded activation only; provider availability and invocation permission are not established.
config.field.provider_invocation_profile: Native invocation profiles and explicit request allocations
cli.help.modelsInvocation:
deckent models invoke|invocation --input <file|-> [--json] [--lang en|tr]
invoke: native command JSON; invocation: persisted receipt query JSON. Both require an explicitly started local `deckent runtime serve`. A runtime-owned invocation continues if the client disconnects; retrying the same command identity returns its receipt and does not resend the native request.
cli.help.modelsPurgeContent:
deckent models purge-content --input <file|-> [--json] [--lang en|tr]
Purges active retained native, usage, or raw response content after separate purge-content policy authorization. It preserves the invocation outcome, quota record, and no-resend identity.
models.invocation.responded: native response content retained separately from the receipt
models.invocation.respondedPurged: native response received; response content has been purged
models.invocation.rejected: rejection content retained separately from the receipt; counts toward the total call quota
models.invocation.rejectedPurged: rejection received; response content has been purged; counts toward the total call quota
models.invocation.unknownPurged: outcome unknown; response content has been purged
models.invocation.notSent: never sent; cancellation {command} prevented dispatch before permission
models.invocation.replayed: Existing receipt returned; request was not sent again.
models.invocation.purgeNotice: Logical purge does not erase write-ahead logs, media, or backups.
models.invocation.noticePurged: A received native response or rejection is evidence only; it is neither task acceptance nor a billing determination. This invocation counts toward the total call quota; retry the same command identity to return its receipt without resending. Response content has been logically purged; human output never shows response content.
models.invocation.notice: A received native response or rejection is evidence only; it is neither task acceptance nor a billing determination. This invocation counts toward the total call quota; retry the same command identity to return its receipt without resending. Response content, if captured, is retained separately from the receipt and withheld by default. JSON includeResponseContent additionally requires inspect-content permission; human output never shows retained response content.
mcp.tool.inspectModelInvocation: Inspect a persisted model invocation with current authorization. It requires an explicitly started local `deckent runtime serve`; a runtime-owned invocation continues if the client disconnects. Response content is withheld by default; JSON includeResponseContent additionally requires inspect-content permission, and human output never shows retained response content.
mcp.tool.purgeModelInvocationContent: Purge active retained native, usage, or raw response content by exact command identity and expected content digest. Requires the local runtime service and separate purge-content policy authorization. It preserves the invocation outcome, quota record, and no-resend identity; logical purge does not erase write-ahead logs, media, or backups.
mcp.tool.invokeModel: Submit one native model request using the configured profile and durable command identity. It requires an explicitly started local `deckent runtime serve`; a runtime-owned invocation continues if the client disconnects. Retrying the same command identity returns its receipt and does not resend the native request. Complete result capacity is checked before a new call. A received native response or rejection is evidence only, neither task acceptance nor a billing determination; the lifetime call is consumed.
mcp.error.modelInvocationResultLimit: The complete result cannot fit this MCP surface. Increase its configured response capacity. For an existing invocation, use SDK or CLI inspection to retrieve the saved result; do not submit a new command to repeat the model call.
